newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says ministers agreed too much oil in market.
newsitem.headline: Iran says ministers agreed too much oil in market.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister said a meeting of seven OPEC ministers in Isfahan on Thursday evening agreed oil markets were oversupplied with crude and they should act quickly to prop up oil prices for the rest of the year.

"Eveybody agreed there is too much crude on the market," Gholamreza Aghazadeh told reporters during an oil and gas conference. "We decided that whoever is overproducing should return to quota and they gave their commitment and it remains to be seen how they will react."
Ministers from Libya, Nigeria, Venezuela, Kuwait, Qatar and Indonesia attended the meeting chaired by Aghazadeh to examine OPEC quota compliance.
"All of the ministers were seriously concerned about the market condition and the deterioration of the crude price, said Aghazadeh.
The minister said it was up to each OPEC member to abide by its output commitment. OPEC has no way of policing quotas.
"Of course within OPEC there is no instrument for creating commitment and it is the political will of the member states to make decisions whether to reduce output or not," he said.
